Sanitopia · Website review, 4 August 2026

The previous site and the
new site, side by side.

Every screenshot below was captured from a real browser at a stated viewport width, not mocked up. Desktop is 1440 px. Mobile is 390 × 844 px at 2× pixel density, which is the iPhone 14 and 15 viewport, using an iPhone user agent and touch input.

What is compared

  • Home page — full reproduction of the previous site
  • Navigation — header and mobile menu
  • Our Projects, Donate, Our Team — content and structure

Where the old pages come from

  • Home and Team: archived captures of 5 and 2 December 2025
  • Our Projects and Donate: Internet Archive captures of 27 and 30 November 2025
  • All rebuilt against the previous theme’s own stylesheet

Navigation · Desktop, 1440px

The header.

The empty boxes in the previous site’s screenshots are its icon font, which the archive did not preserve. On the live site those rendered as a heart and social glyphs. Nothing else is affected.

Previous site

Four top-level items: About, Our Projects, Nkonya SHS, News. Donate Now plus four social icons sit to the right. Gallery is reachable only inside the Nkonya SHS dropdown. There is no Contact link and no route to Partner in Ghana.

New site

A slim strapline bar states the legal status on every page. Five top-level items, with Our Projects opening onto the four individual projects. Contact sits beside a square Donate button.

Home page · Desktop, 1440px

The first screen a partner sees.

Previous site

The screen opens on the logo, a donate button and social icons. Below them sits a three-photograph carousel, fading every five seconds inside a narrow column. It carries no words; the headline sits separately underneath, set in all capitals, centred.

New site

A photograph from the Nkonya commissioning fills the screen inside a purple mat, carrying a two-word headline. Five such covers rotate, each from a real project.

03
Home page · iPhone, 390 × 844

On a phone, the difference is not subtle.

Previous site

The whole first screen is furniture: logo, hamburger, a full-width Donate Now bar and a row of social icons that runs off the right-hand edge. The photograph is letterboxed below it, and the headline then takes four lines of capitals.

New site

The photograph is the screen. Logo and menu button sit on one slim row above it, the headline sits on the image, and the slide counter shows there are five. Nothing overflows the width.

Previous site

Headed Contacts — Get in Touch with Us. Four ways to give are described — one-off donation, fundraiser, essential supplies and $20,000 sponsorship — but each one ends in the same generic enquiry form, repeated three times down the page. There is no payment route.

The argument

Why the new site is better on a phone.

Most people who look Sanitopia up will do it on a phone, often after seeing a post or being sent a link. These are the differences that matter at that width.

✗Previous site on an iPhone

  • It scrolled sideways. Every page measured 394 px against a 390 px screen, so the page drifted left and right under the thumb
  • The social icons were cut off by the right edge of the screen, on every page
  • The first screen carried no photograph. Logo, a donate bar and social icons filled it before any content began
  • Headlines were set in capitals and ran to four lines, which is slower to read and takes most of a phone screen for a few words
  • The desktop layout was simply narrowed rather than rethought, so text ran the full width of the screen with no measure
  • Its three-photograph carousel sat boxed below the header furniture and carried no words, so the pictures said nothing on their own

✓New site on an iPhone

  • Zero overflow on all four pages measured. The page cannot drift sideways
  • The photograph is the first screen, the same cover a partner sees on a laptop
  • Headlines are two or three words in mixed case, sized to fit one screen
  • Everything reflows: four-column grids become two, three-column grids become one, and the gallery strip scrolls sideways deliberately
  • The menu carries the social links, which on the old site were only in a row that did not fit
  • Tap targets are full-width rows in the menu rather than small inline links
  • A five-slide cover carousel fills the screen, and every slide carries its own headline, with a counter and progress dots
11
Beyond layout

What the new site carries that the old one did not.

Recovered

  • All six directors with full biographies and portraits
  • The image library, expanded to 284 photographs
  • News posts restored with their true publication dates
  • Company registration and registered office in the footer, as a CIC must publish

Added

  • The George Padmore Research Library commissioning
  • The Asikuma facility, absent from the old site entirely
  • The 10,000 by 2035 mission, with national press cited
  • The HealthFab partnership and the ministerial plaque unveiling

Structural

  • Clean URLs throughout, with the old addresses redirected rather than broken
  • Named institutional partners on the home page, which is the first thing a funder looks for
  • A single route to engage: partner, donate, memoir, gifts in kind
  • Delivery commitments stated as numbers: 120 days, 80%, 100%, zero
12
Method and limitations

How this was put together.

What was done

  • Both sites were loaded in the same browser engine at the same two viewport sizes
  • Mobile captures use a 390 × 844 viewport at 2× density with an iPhone user agent and touch enabled
  • Scroll-triggered animations were forced open so nothing was captured mid-fade
  • Overflow figures are read from the browser’s own layout, not estimated by eye

What to be careful about

  • The previous site’s home page is a complete reproduction, including its own page stylesheet. Its screenshots and measurements are faithful
  • Our Projects, Donate and Our Team are reproductions whose page-specific stylesheet the archive did not preserve. Their text, images and structure are exact; some spacing and image placement is not. They are shown to compare content, not pixels
  • The empty boxes in the old screenshots are its icon font, which the archive did not keep. They rendered normally on the live site
  • The black strip at the top of each old screenshot is a label added to the reproduction so it can never be mistaken for the live site
  • Analytics and payment scripts were removed from the reproductions. They do not affect layout
Captured 4 August 2026. Previous site: home 5 December 2025, team 2 December 2025, Our Projects 27 November 2025, Donate 30 November 2025.
